raw_draft.tldr:
The tariff channel is real and the record confirms it: US soybean exports fell to 41.37 MMT in 2025/26 from 51.49 MMT in 2024/25 [N164][N163] while Brazil's rose to 115 MMT from 103.14 MMT [N159][N158] -- the flow rerouted rather than disappeared. But the balance sheet did NOT loosen with it: US stocks-to-use sits at 10.72% of domestic use for 2026/27 [N81], the 23rd percentile of its own record [N83] and falling three marketing years running, and the weekly shipment pace has recovered from its August 2026 trough at the 3rd percentile [N116] to the 62nd [N115]. On the readings above, seven point toward a higher price and six toward a lower beside a November 2026 settle of 1,317.5 US cents/bushel [N120] at the 97th percentile of that contract's own sessions since June 2025 [N125] and up 176 cents over sixty-three sessions [N124] -- my lean is modestly toward higher prices, tempered because the single reading furthest from its own record, a tropical Pacific sea-surface temperature anomaly of +1.8 degC [N33], is declared to push this market the other way.

## Mechanism

**The tariff channel.** Chinese duties on US-origin beans do not destroy demand; they reroute it to Brazil, depressing the US export channel that the CBOT benchmark prices off. That is the model's high-confidence mechanism, and the tariff-driven demand-loss pattern needs two of its four conditions. On this read none are showing, and one reads the opposite way -- the shipment pace [N113] is running ahead, which counts against the pattern.

**What offsets it.** A tight stocks-to-use buffer is where the convexity lives: at the 23rd percentile [N83] and past the line the desk calls tight, a supply shock has little cushion to absorb it, so the right tail is fatter than the left. Against that, a warm-phase Pacific at +1.8 degC [N33], +2.4 sigma on its trailing ten years [N34], is declared to move this market in the opposite direction at medium confidence with a one-to-two-quarter lag -- its effect window, counted from the July 2026 reading, closes around January 2027. Argentine production of 50 MMT for 2026/27 [N93] and US harvested area of 34.76 M ha [N101 at the 91st percentile] lean the same loosening way.

**The crush leg.** The board crush margin at 2.43 USD/bu [N102], 89th percentile of its record since September 2021 [N104], having peaked at the 96th in July 2026 [N105], pulls bean demand forward. Four declared upstream paths (crude, the Renewable Fuel Standard, biodiesel mandates) land on this one reading, so it is one risk, not four.

## The record

**The chain, link by link.** From the tariff to the balance sheet: no series is served at the tariff link itself, so the first hop is documented, not measured -- the WASDE of 12 May 2026 projected US exports rising to 1.630 billion bushels in 2026/27 against a 2025/26 when tariff measures curtailed shipments to China [E26]. Next link, shipments [N113] bottomed at the 3rd percentile [N116] in August 2026 and now read the 62nd [N115]; the model expects a slow pace to loosen the stocks ratio, and the readings agree. Final link, that ratio [N81] sits at the 23rd percentile [N83], falling since 2023. The record here is thin: shipments sat this far out four times before, and on none of them was a stocks-ratio reading published inside the lag the model allows, and this contract's price record does not reach those episodes.

**Timing, from the dated items.** China imposed 25 percent duties in spring 2018 [E1], specifically on 6 July 2018 [E2]; the WASDE flagged the trade effect on 12 July 2018 [E3]; the exclusion process returning duties from 30.5 to 3 percent took effect 2 March 2020 [E23]. The 2018 price effect showed within the same quarter -- faster than the model's zero-to-two-quarter prior -- with the November 2018 delivery down 167.5 cents, or -16.14%, from 1 March to 14 November 2018 [N18], and managed money swinging -192,126 contracts over that stretch to -14,295 [N21][N13]. Retaliatory duties were reported again on 19 March 2025 [E7].

**Prices and positioning now.** The season-average farm price, a USDA in-year estimate and not a futures settle, rose from $10.00/bu in 2024/25 [N169] to $10.50/bu in 2025/26 [N170]. Managed money is 265,159 contracts [N42], the 100th percentile of its record since August 2023 [N44] -- at the end of its own record. The model reads a position that far out this way: large net length amplifies and can overextend price moves, while extreme positioning flags reversal risk. That is the model's reading, not an added forecast of mine.

**A past episode, for coincidence only.** Over the October-December 2021 window on the record, one delivery month held at both ends, beans settled +3.03% [N171], soybean meal +20.31% [N175] -- the declared crush relation held, in-sample on that window. Meal-to-oil: oil settled -13.86% [N176], the declared opposite-direction relation held. Oil-to-palm: palm settled -9.29% [N177]; that relation is declared same-direction and the read states it held on the window. Rapeseed meal +10.21% [N172] and rapeseed oil +3.88% [N174], each a move inside Chinese yuan against beans' move inside US dollars, no rate applied; the yuan per dollar moved -1.1% over the same window [N173]. MATIF rapeseed cannot be read -- that window predates the board's own price history. That window ended four years before this as-of, and it settles only that these relations coincided then.

## Where the record disagrees

The flow rerouted between countries over one shared window, MY2024 to MY2025, and must not be blended:
- Brazil: exports 103.14 MMT [N158] to 115 MMT [N159], a change of +11.858 MMT [N160], +11.5% [N161]
- United States: exports 51.49 MMT [N163] to 41.37 MMT [N164], a change of -10.127 MMT [N165], -19.67% [N166]
Brazil's 2026/27 exports read 118 MMT [N162], the 99th percentile of its own record [N53].

## What to watch

- **The Pacific warm phase [N33]** -- +1.8 degC, July 2026, eight months rising, past the line the desk calls strong at one and a half degC; declared to pressure this market with its window running 2026-10-31 to 2027-01-31. Wrong if the next print, due between 1 and 5 October 2026, turns back inside that line or the run breaks.
- **US stocks-to-use [N81]** -- 10.72% for 2026/27, read 11 September 2026, three years falling, past the line called tight at the 25th percentile; this is the buffer that makes any supply shock convex. Wrong if the next print, 9-12 October 2026, turns back inside that line.
- **The board crush margin [N102]** -- 2.43 USD/bu, 23 September 2026, with four declared upstream paths landing on it; window open to 23 December 2026. Wrong if the next print returns it to the middle of its own record, which takes the move off every path at once.
- **Weekly shipments [N113]** -- three weeks rising, past the line called ahead, window to 17 December 2026; this is the tariff channel's live readout. Wrong if the next print, 1 October 2026, turns back inside that line. I take this in place of a crude-oil item: crude at 0.51 z [N106] has fallen back to the 68th percentile [N108] from a 98th-percentile April 2026 peak [N109], so it is doing less work here, and I leave the Brazil-export and Thailand-import tail readings aside as second-order to the tariff question asked.

Coverage, honestly: the newest dated document behind this answer is 12 May 2026, the newest figure was known 28 September 2026, and the price tape runs through 28 September 2026 -- so the documentary layer is the thin one on the 2026 tariff leg.
